statement: People outdoors is a step between heat and shootings in New York City: daily 311 Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints, a proxy for street activity, rise with the day's maximum temperature, and adding them to the daily model removes at least a quarter of the temperature slope of shootings.

graph_evidence.summary: Graph sign for the first link is negative. Kim et al. 2022 (Korea Community Health Survey 2018): odds of walking practice 0.95 (0.94 to 0.97) per 1 C of the preceding week's daily maximum in rural areas and 0.98 (0.97 to 1.00) in urban areas; the graph holds the rural value only. The second association returned (walking after fan precooling, rectal temperature) is a laboratory finding on body temperature and is noise here.

The relationship aggregates report 13 findings; the API returns one. Mora-Rodriguez et al. 2016 (573 adults, Spain, Greece, Germany): self-reported physical activity falls with ambient temperature, r = -0.277.

Ten laboratory findings on exercise time, intensity and heart rate in hot versus temperate chambers, signs mixed (6 plus, 3 minus); grounded to the concept 'hot'. They concern capacity under heat stress, not whether people are outdoors. Not read in abstract; not relied on.

Six of seven findings are negative and run from crime to walking (fear of crime, crime safety, violent crime reduce walking). The graph holds no finding that more people walking or outdoors raises violence; the second arrow of this pathway is absent from the graph.

concepts: violence side: violence, crime, aggression, anger, irritability, hostility, intimate partner violence
graph_evidence.summary: Eight of nine negative: neighbourhood crime lowers physical activity, and active adolescents report less fighting. Again the reverse direction or an individual trait, not a daily exposure effect.

Found only through variable names. Potgieter et al. 2022, Khayelitsha, South Africa, 2006-2016: days at or above 25 C raise the cumulative relative risk of violent crime by up to 32% (the graph stores RR 1.32 without an interval; the abstract gives none). A direct heat-violence finding that the concept search for temperature and violence did not return.

literature.finding: NYC daily shooting incidents: IRR 1.146 (1.130 to 1.163) per 5 C TMAX; the spline keeps rising to 35 C.

literature.citation: Reeping PM, Hemenway D. Inj Epidemiol 2020;7:31.
literature.finding: Chicago shootings rise with temperature more on weekends and holidays, read by the authors as routine activity.

prediction.magnitude: First link: IRR of daily Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints per 5 C TMAX between 1.15 and 1.45. The graph predicts the opposite sign for outdoor activity in heat (walking OR 0.95 to 0.98 per 1 C, activity r = -0.28); I expect the graph's sign to appear only at the hot end, as a flattening: the spline RR of the mediator rises less from 27 to 33 C than from 15 to 21 C, and for the bicycle counts the RR at 33 C is at or below the RR at 27 C, while the shootings curve (already seen) rises 12% from 27 to 33 C. Attenuation A between 0.10 and 0.35 for the noise proxy.
prediction.support_if: confirmed: the mediator's IRR per 5 C has a lower limit above 1, its coefficient in B1 is positive with a lower limit above 0, and A >= 0.25 with the lower bootstrap limit above 0.10.
prediction.refute_if: contested: A < 0.10 with the upper bootstrap limit below 0.25, or the mediator does not rise with temperature (upper limit of its IRR at or below 1). Anything else is unsettled.

plan: Primary mediator: daily count of 311 service requests with complaint_type 'Noise - Street/Sidewalk' by created_date, from 76ig-c548 (2010-2019) and erm2-nwe9 (2020 to present), 2010-01-01 to 2026-08-31. Secondary mediator, reported but not deciding: daily bicycle counts from ct66-47at (travelmode bike), summed over the sensors that report on at least 90% of the analysed days of a calendar year, year by year, 2014 to 2026; if the aggregation query does not complete, this is reported as not done. The shape comparison (spline RR at 27 and 33 C) is reported for both and is descriptive. Daily series for New York City. Shootings (5ucz-vwe8, distinct incident_key per occur_date), Central Park TMAX and PRCP (GHCN-Daily USW00094728) and the calendar terms are built exactly as in analyses/heat/shootings.py. Base model B0: negative binomial GLM of daily shooting incidents on TMAX/5, day of week, calendar month, year, holiday and rain >= 1 mm (alpha by ML, HC0 errors), refitted on the days for which the mediator exists. First link L1: the same model with the mediator's daily count as the outcome, giving the mediator's IRR per 5 C; and the same with a natural cubic spline of TMAX (4 df) to read the mediator's RR at 21, 27 and 33 C against 15 C. Mediator model B1: B0 plus log(1 + mediator count) on the same day. Attenuation A = 1 - b1/b0, where b0 and b1 are the coefficients of TMAX/5 in B0 and B1. Interval for A: 500 bootstrap resamples of calendar weeks (all seven days of a week kept together), alpha held at its full-sample value, 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. This is mediation by proxy and not identification: the proxy measures the mediator with error, which pulls A toward zero; an unmeasured cause of both the mediator and shootings that is correlated with temperature pushes A upward; and conditioning on a mediator can open a path through such a cause. Pre-specified sensitivity, the same for every mediator: (s1) year-by-month fixed effects in place of month and year; (s2) 2020 and 2021 excluded; (s3) warm season May to September only; (s4) mediator on the previous day in place of the same day. If A under s1 falls on the other side of a decision threshold from the primary A, the verdict is unsettled. Already seen by the project before this registration: the daily shootings and Central Park temperature series and their relation (heat-shootings: IRR 1.146 per 5 C, 1.130 to 1.163; spline RR against the median TMAX 1.37 at 27 C, 1.46 at 30 C, 1.54 at 33 C); daily FDNY EMS dispatches of type SHOT, T-SHOT and STAB (bridge-shot-ems-link, bridge-heat-shootings-ems); the 2023 totals of EMS dispatches by initial call type (DRUG 88,621; EDP 98,371); 311 noise complaints of 2022-2024 summed by latitude and longitude, not by day (nbhd-noise311-exposure); daily 311 street-flooding complaints (further-tidal-flooding-311); and, for this registration, the number of rows and sensors per year and travel mode in ct66-47at (no count values). No daily series of 311 Noise - Street/Sidewalk, 311 Drinking, EMS DRUG or EDP dispatches, or bicycle counts has been queried or seen.
alternatives: Noise complaints rise in heat because windows are open and complainants are at home, not because more people are on the street; the proxy then overstates the first link.
Complaints and shootings share causes other than temperature within a month (block parties, holidays, the summer of 2020); sensitivity s1 and s2 address part of this.
Physiology (irritability, sleep loss) acts on the same days; a positive A does not exclude it, and a small A may reflect a poor proxy.
Bicycle counts on bridges and commuter routes measure travel, not people lingering outdoors at night when most shootings occur.
